jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 23799 

Department: Finance and Corporate Services Dept.

Service: Information Technology Services

Employment Type: 1 Full Time Permanent Position 

Work Hours: 35.00 /hours per week

Affiliation: MPE/New City MPE

Salary Information: $174,164.90 - $220,256.40  annually (2025 rates of pay)

Location: 100 Constellation, Nepean  

Job Category: Management 

Application Close: 23/10/2026

Job Summary

You are accountable for providing corporate leadership and strategic planning for the City's information technology function in support of City operations, corporate priorities and the delivery of municipal programs and services.

You are accountable for the leadership, delivery and continuous improvement of the Service's priorities, services, programs and operations, including enterprise technology and artificial intelligence strategy and governance, technology architecture, roadmaps and investment planning, enterprise applications and digital capabilities, technology infrastructure and asset management, and workplace technology and user support services.

You provide strategic technology and artificial intelligence advice to the General Manager, City Manager, senior leaders and Council on matters affecting technology services, digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, investments, risks and organizational priorities. You ensure information security, privacy, data governance, accessibility, ethical use and digital risk requirements are integrated into technology and artificial intelligence strategies, investments, services and operational practices.

You are also accountable for the effective management of the Service’s human and financial resources, including contracted services, and for maintaining productive relationships with internal and external partners while fostering corporate alignment, continuous improvement and service excellence.

Education And Experience

Completion of 4 year university degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, Public Administration or other related field.

Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible senior leadership experience in technology and artificial intelligence strategy, governance, digital transformation, service delivery, enterprise applications and technology infrastructure within a large, complex public-sector or comparable environment, including a minimum of 5 years leading multidisciplinary teams, organizational change and adoption, external contract resources, and operating and capital budgets.

KNOWLEDGE

Principles, practices, legislation, regulations, standards and governance frameworks related to information technology services, programs and operations
Enterprise technology strategy, governance, architecture, roadmaps and investment planning
Enterprise applications and digital capabilities, technology infrastructure and asset management, workplace technology and user support services
Industry trends, emerging technologies, developments, leading practices and service delivery models
Artificial intelligence technologies, enterprise AI platforms, adoption approaches, operating models and lifecycle management
Responsible AI principles and governance, including human oversight, transparency, fairness, accessibility, privacy, security, data governance, records management, procurement and risk management
Enterprise AI adoption and enablement practices, including use-case evaluation, prioritization, implementation, performance measurement and value realization
Organizational change management, workforce enablement, digital literacy and technology adoption practices
Information security, privacy and digital risk principles and requirements as they relate to technology services and operations
Public sector governance, public administration, policy development and business administration principles and practices
Principles and methods of economic, financial, social and political risk analysis
Project management principles and practices
The City of Ottawa, its operations, corporate governance structure, priorities and decision-making processes
Relevant legislation, regulations, City policies and procedures
Public-private partnerships and other alternative service delivery models
Human resource management practices in a unionized work environment
Must be familiar with applicable health and safety legislation, have knowledge of any potential or actual danger to health or safety in the workplace, and have knowledge of appropriate actions to be taken to ensure the health and safety of staff in accordance with applicable legislation and City policies and procedures

Competencies, Skills And Abilities

Core Behaviours

Core behaviours define the City's expectations of the behaviours employees should demonstrate in performing their work. They are reflective of the City's culture and values and guide all our present and future activities. Every employee is encouraged to learn, embody, and demonstrate these core behaviours.

Review the Core Behaviours .

Leadership Competencies

The City has defined key competencies that leaders are expected to embody and demonstrate to successfully move the organization towards achieving its strategic objectives and create an organizational culture that supports and empowers employees to excel, grow and reach their full potential. These leadership competencies and associated behaviours are expected to be demonstrated by leaders at all levels of the organization.

Review the Leadership Competencies .

What You Need To Know

Language Requirement: This is a designated day-1 ready bilingual position as per the City of Ottawa’s Bilingualism Policy and fluency in both of Canada’s official languages is required and a language assessment will be completed as part of the selection process. In exceptional circumstances, and subject to Council approval, internal and external candidates that do not meet the language requirement may be considered.
Experience and formal training combined with demonstrated performance and ability may substitute for stipulated academic requirements.
Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.

We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

The City of Ottawa promotes the principles of diversity and inclusion and adheres to the tenets of the Canadian Human Rights Act and the Ontario Human Rights Code. We encourage applications from members of Indigenous, Black and other racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women and non-binary persons, persons of all ethnic origins, religions, sexual orientations, classes, gender identities and expressions.

Candidates are encouraged to self-identify as a member of one or more designated employment equity groups in the self-identification questionnaire.

The City of Ottawa provides accommodation to applicants during all parts of the hiring process, upon request. If contacted to proceed to the selection process, please advise us if you require any accommodation.

Accessible formats and communication supports are available upon request. Please contact the HR Service Centre (email: HRServiceCentre@Ottawa.ca) at 613-580-2424, extension 47411 Employee Service Centre at 613-580-2424 extension 12211 or via email at esc-cse@ottawa.ca .

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Serv, a global executive recruitment partner, is hiring on behalf of our client Martell Ventures for a Chief Technology Officer.

Join the Team:
The Martell Group exists to build people, brands, and ventures that create meaningful impact. Founded by serial entrepreneur and investor Dan Martell, we combine audience, operators, and execution to launch and scale products in Media, B2B SaaS, and AI.

Martell Ventures is a software and AI company that happens to have two services companies in it. Dan is also an investor in companies like Udemy, Intercom, and Unbounce. Our values: Build the people. Be the example. Simple scales.

For more information, visit: https://www.danmartell.com/
Why you shouldn't work here: Radical Transparency from our CEO

Position Responsibilities:
Martell Ventures is looking for a highly technical builder and strategic thinker to lead engineering excellence across its growing portfolio of businesses.

This is not a traditional CTO role focused solely on executive oversight. We need someone who can think strategically, challenge assumptions, and get directly involved in the technical work when it matters most.

You will be the technical authority across the Ventures portfolio, helping companies build better products, solve complex engineering challenges, strengthen technical teams, and move faster with modern AI and agentic development.

You'll work closely with Dan Martell, portfolio business leaders, and experienced technology advisors to turn ambitious ideas into practical, scalable solutions.

A significant part of your mandate will be establishing Martell Ventures' technical presence in Waterloo, building a strong local engineering community, and creating the standards that enable our portfolio companies to scale.

This is an opportunity to shape how multiple businesses build, operate, and grow while remaining close to the technology itself.

This role includes:
Technical Strategy & Architecture
Evaluate the technical infrastructure, architecture, codebases, and engineering practices across portfolio companies, identifying opportunities to improve quality, security, scalability, and performance.
Work directly with engineering teams to diagnose technical challenges, improve architecture, and implement practical solutions.
Establish consistent engineering standards, shared development practices, frameworks, and tooling across the portfolio.
Drive adoption of modern AI and agentic development practices to improve engineering speed, efficiency, and product delivery.
Ensure portfolio companies maintain appropriate technical infrastructure, security practices, backups, and operational resilience.
Help portfolio leaders understand technical risks, opportunities, and priorities so they can make informed business decisions.
Support technical readiness for future acquisitions, investment opportunities, and potential exits.

Building & Developing Technical Talent
Establish and grow Martell Ventures' technical presence in Kitchener-Waterloo.
Help recruit, assess, and develop exceptional engineering talent across the portfolio.
Partner with portfolio business leaders on technical hiring decisions, including engineering leads and senior technical positions.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to portfolio engineering leaders while maintaining a dotted-line relationship with those leaders.
Establish consistent technical practices, knowledge-sharing, and training opportunities across portfolio teams.
Develop relationships with the University of Waterloo, Communitech, and the broader Waterloo technology ecosystem to build a sustainable talent pipeline.
Collaborate with Waterloo-based technology advisors Michael Litt and Marcelo Cortes to strengthen the group's engineering capabilities and local network.

Product Development & Execution
Translate ambitious business ideas into practical technical plans with clear priorities, realistic timelines, and measurable outcomes.
Provide hands-on technical support when portfolio companies face complex engineering challenges or execution bottlenecks.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions and help prioritize technical investments based on business value.
Support engineering teams in delivering reliable, scalable products that meet customer needs.
Identify opportunities to share technical capabilities, infrastructure, and resources across portfolio businesses.
Balance long-term technical architecture with the immediate needs of fast-moving businesses.

Strategic Partnership & Leadership
Serve as a trusted technical thought partner to Dan Martell and the Ventures leadership team.
Bring independent technical judgment, including the confidence to challenge ideas, push back on unrealistic commitments, and recommend alternative approaches.
Help establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Work across multiple businesses and priorities while maintaining a clear focus on the highest-impact opportunities.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, and progress clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Lead by example through a combination of strategic thinking, practical execution, and strong technical credibility.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone with exceptional technical depth, strong product judgment, and the ability to build in fast-moving environments.
You may have held a CTO or VP of Engineering position, or you may be an exceptional Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or technical founder ready to take on broader responsibility.

What matters most is your ability to solve difficult technical problems, raise engineering standards, and build products that work.
Deep hands-on experience in software engineering, systems architecture, and building scalable production applications.
Recent, practical experience developing with modern AI technologies, LLMs, agents, and agentic development tools.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate existing software architecture, identify technical weaknesses, and implement effective solutions.
Strong technical credibility and the ability to work directly with experienced engineers on complex technical challenges.
Experience building and shipping software products in startup, scale-up, or similarly fast-moving environments.
Strong product and business judgment, with an understanding of how technical decisions affect customers, revenue, and growth.
Experience assessing engineering talent, making technical hiring decisions, and helping build high-performing teams.
Ability to balance technical quality with speed, pragmatism, and commercial priorities.
Confidence working with strong founder personalities and challenging ideas when necessary.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business recommendations.
High ownership, adaptability, and comfort operating across multiple businesses with changing priorities.
Based in, or willing to relocate to, Kitchener-Waterloo and work in person full-time.

Nice-to-Haves
Previous experience as a CTO, technical co-founder, VP of Engineering, or senior technical leader.
Experience supporting multiple products, portfolio companies, or venture-backed businesses.
Experience building or scaling an engineering function from an early stage.
Involvement in a successful company exit or technical due diligence process.
Existing connections within the Waterloo technology ecosystem, including the University of Waterloo or Communitech.
Experience establishing engineering standards and shared infrastructure across multiple teams.

Our Dream Teammate Is Someone Who:
Is a builder at heart and genuinely enjoys getting into the technical details.
Is excited by the pace of change in AI and is actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Can move comfortably between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
Knows when to challenge an idea, when to simplify a solution, and when to move quickly.
Has strong technical opinions but remains open to learning and feedback.
Thrives in entrepreneurial environments where priorities evolve and ownership matters.
Is proactive and accountable.
Thinks strategically and executes consistently.
Communicates with clarity and confidence.
Brings a positive, growth-oriented mindset.
Is highly organized and dependable.
Cares deeply about building great products and developing great people.

Hiring Process
We take our hiring process seriously and evaluate candidates based on both capability and culture fit. Our goal is to ensure you step into a role where you feel genuinely excited and fulfilled. That's important for you, and it's equally important for us.

Below is a snapshot of what you can expect throughout our hiring process.

Please note that steps may vary slightly depending on the position.
Initial application review and introductory conversation with Serv.
Leadership and culture-fit conversation with Martell Ventures.
Technical evaluation with members of the Martell Ventures technical leadership or advisory network.
Final-stage conversations with key stakeholders.

Location
Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Canada

This is a full-time, in-person position. The CTO will play a central role in establishing and leading Martell Ventures' Waterloo technical hub.

Compensation
$150,000- $250,000 CAD base, based on experience.

The opportunity also includes a proposed portfolio-level phantom equity component designed to align long-term incentives with the performance and success of the Ventures portfolio. Final terms are subject to confirmation.
This isn't just a job. It's a platform to build, grow, and win.

Serv uses AI tools in our recruitment process, including developing job postings and note-taking during interviews. AI is not used to screen, assess, or select candidates. All resumes are reviewed by a human, and all hiring decisions are made by humans. Any AI-generated output used during the recruitment process is reviewed by a human before action is taken.

jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Go-to-Market Sales
jobs.description:
The Role

We are seeking a Vice President, Enterprise Go-to-Market to own and scale our enterprise growth strategy across sales, offerings, strategic partnerships, and go-to-market execution.

This is a player-coach role designed for an experienced services executive who is equally comfortable building strategy and personally driving revenue. Initially, the VP will operate primarily as an individual contributor with one direct report, personally leading strategic pursuits and establishing the foundation for a broader enterprise GTM organization as the business scales.

This role will own the enterprise motion across the board: identifying where we should play, developing differentiated offerings, activating our technology partnerships, building pipeline, leading complex sales cycles, and creating the operating rigor required to forecast and grow the business predictably.

Enterprise Go-to-Market Leadership

Own the enterprise GTM strategy, operating plan, pipeline, bookings, and revenue performance
Develop and execute account and territory strategies for strategic enterprise customers
Personally originate, develop, and close complex consulting and technology-services opportunities
Establish a repeatable enterprise sales motion that can scale as the organization grows
Partner with executive leadership across sales, marketing, delivery, solutions, and operations to translate growth priorities into executable GTM plans
Maintain direct ownership of a meaningful revenue quota and demonstrate consistent performance against bookings targets

Offering & Solution Development

Identify market opportunities and translate them into differentiated, commercially viable service offerings
Build compelling propositions at the intersection of consulting, implementation, transformation, AI, CRM, commerce, and agreement management
Define positioning, packaging, pricing, target customers, partner alignment, and sales enablement for new offerings
Work closely with delivery and technical leaders to ensure offerings are both market-relevant and operationally executable
Continuously evaluate customer demand, competitive dynamics, partner priorities, and emerging technologies to evolve the portfolio

Strategic Partnerships

Develop and manage executive-level relationships across our strategic technology ecosystem
Create joint GTM strategies with partners that generate sourced and influenced pipeline
Navigate partner organizations to build relationships across sales, alliances, product, industry, and field leadership
Translate partner priorities into actionable account mapping, campaigns, offerings, and co-selling motions
Experience working within ecosystems including ServiceNow, Salesforce, Anthropic, DocuSign, CPQ and commerce platforms is strongly preferred

Sales Execution & Operating Discipline

Lead sophisticated enterprise sales cycles from opportunity identification through qualification, solution development, commercial negotiation, and close
Establish strong opportunity management, pipeline progression, and CRM discipline
Ensure CRM data accurately reflects pipeline health, deal progression, next actions, risk, and forecast
Build executive-level reporting around pipeline, bookings, win rate, sales velocity, conversion, forecast accuracy, and other critical GTM metrics
Analyze sales data to identify trends, risks, productivity issues, and opportunities for improvement
Produce reliable weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasts and clearly communicate assumptions and risks to executive leadership

Leadership

Initially manage one direct report while operating as a hands-on enterprise seller and GTM leader
Provide leadership and influence across the broader commercial organization without relying on organizational hierarchy
Establish processes, standards, and operating rhythms that can support a larger enterprise organization over time
Coach team members on enterprise selling, account strategy, partner engagement, opportunity management, and commercial discipline
Help define the future organizational structure and talent requirements for enterprise growth

Requirements

What We're Looking For

Significant experience selling and leading professional services, consulting, digital transformation, or technology implementation services into enterprise organizations
Demonstrated history of personally carrying and consistently achieving or exceeding a significant revenue quota
Experience building enterprise pipeline and closing complex, multi-stakeholder opportunities
Strong understanding of CRM, CPQ, commerce, digital transformation, AI, and enterprise technology ecosystems
Meaningful experience with several of the following platforms and ecosystems:
ServiceNow
Salesforce
Anthropic and enterprise AI
DocuSign
CPQ and quote-to-cash technologies
Commerce platforms including commercetools, Shopify, BigCommerce, or comparable enterprise platforms

Proven ability to develop new service offerings and successfully take them to market
Experience creating and executing partner-led and co-sell GTM strategies
Strong command of CRM systems, pipeline management, forecasting, and sales operations
Highly analytical; able to move comfortably between individual opportunities and aggregate business performance
Experience presenting pipeline, forecast, performance, and GTM strategy to executive leadership
Strong commercial judgment with the ability to balance revenue growth, delivery feasibility, margin, and strategic value
Comfortable operating in a high-growth environment where the expectation is to build while selling, rather than inherit a fully developed organization
Success in This Role
Success will be measured by the VP's ability to create a predictable, scalable enterprise growth engine—not simply manage an existing sales team
The successful candidate will generate and close meaningful enterprise revenue, improve pipeline quality and forecast accuracy, create differentiated offerings, deepen strategic technology partnerships, and establish the processes and discipline necessary to scale the enterprise GTM organization
This role is ideal for someone who has already led at the VP level but still wants to be close to customers, partners, deals, and the market. We are looking for a builder and seller—not an administrator

Benefits

Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Plan (401k, IRA)
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
Short Term & Long Term Disability
Training & Development
Work From Home
Wellness Resources

jobs.title: Director, Applications, Data & Integration
jobs.description:
Job Description

Our client is seeking an experienced and strategic Director, Applications, Data & Integration to join a growing Digital Business Services team. This leadership role is responsible for building and leading enterprise application, data, and integration capabilities while driving modernization through AI-assisted engineering, modern DevOps practices, and enterprise data management. The position plays a key role in the organization's long-term digital and technology transformation strategy.

Responsibilities

Applications & Software Engineering Leadership

Provide technical leadership and architecture oversight across the enterprise application landscape.
Establish application architecture, development, and lifecycle standards.
Guide solution design for new applications and major enhancements.
Partner with Product Owners to translate business requirements into sustainable technical solutions.
Provide technical oversight of implementation partners and third-party development resources.
Build and mature software engineering practices, including development standards, source control, code reviews, testing, and documentation.
Establish CI/CD, environment management, and release management capabilities to support controlled and repeatable deployments.
Embed application security and secure development practices throughout the software development lifecycle.
Lead adoption of AI-assisted development practices to accelerate development, testing, documentation, and delivery.
Drive significant improvements in engineering productivity while maintaining security, quality, and appropriate human oversight.
Strengthen automated testing, application monitoring, and overall technical quality.

Integration Architecture

Own enterprise integration architecture and technical integration standards.
Establish consistent approaches for APIs, interfaces, and system-to-system data exchange.
Ensure integrations across the application landscape are secure, resilient, supportable, and appropriately monitored.
Maintain an architectural view of how applications, integrations, and data work together across the enterprise.

Enterprise Applications & Platform Leadership

Provide technical leadership for enterprise business platforms, including Microsoft Dynamics 365 and related technologies.
Work with Product Owners and implementation partners on architecture, integration, and technical design.
Build sufficient internal capability to support, maintain, and extend business platforms over time.
Ensure platform development aligns with engineering, security, and application management standards.

Data & Analytics

Develop enterprise data architecture and technical data management practices.
Build data engineering capabilities to integrate, transform, and make trusted data available across the organization.
Establish approaches for master data management, data quality, lineage, and technical controls.
Build and lead emerging data engineering and analytics capabilities.
Enable consistent enterprise reporting and analytics.
Partner with business stakeholders on data ownership and governance.

People Leadership

Build and lead teams spanning application development, integration, quality assurance, data engineering, and analytics.
Develop technical staff and establish clear engineering expectations and practices.
Determine the appropriate balance of internal capabilities, implementation partners, and specialized contractors.
Foster a culture focused on technical quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and effective use of AI-assisted development.

Security & Operational Excellence

Partner with IT Operations to ensure applications and integrations meet security, resilience, and operational requirements.
Embed security-by-design principles into application architecture and engineering practices.
Ensure solutions incorporate appropriate access controls, data protection, monitoring, and operational support requirements.

Qualifications

Required

Progressive technology leadership experience across enterprise applications, software engineering, integration, and data.
Demonstrated experience building or maturing software engineering and DevOps practices.
Strong understanding of modern application architecture, APIs, integrations, and cloud platforms.
Practical experience with CI/CD, automated testing, secure development, and application lifecycle management.
Experience adopting modern development practices and AI-assisted development tools to improve engineering productivity and software delivery.
Experience with data architecture, data engineering, analytics, or business intelligence.
Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and external technology partners.
Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical teams and business leaders.

Preferred

Experience with Microsoft technologies, including Dynamics 365 and the broader Microsoft ecosystem.
Experience leading enterprise technology modernization, digital transformation, or platform modernization initiatives.

jobs.title: Chief Courts Information Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Business Data Office, Data Integrity & Operations
jobs.description:
Experience something Brilliantly Different with MUFG Investor Services.  

MUFG Investor Services is a trusted partner to many of the world’s largest public and private funds, providing asset servicing and operational solutions built for alternatives. With over $1 trillion in client assets under administration, we offer fund administration, banking, payments, fund financing, foreign exchange overlay, corporate and regulatory services, custody, business consulting, and more. Operating from 17 locations worldwide, we help clients mitigate risk, enhance efficiency, and navigate the operational complexities of today’s investment management landscape. As a division of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s largest financial institutions with approximately $3 trillion in assets, we combine deep expertise with the strength and stability of a leading financial institution.

To learn more, visit us at www.mufg-investorservices.com.

Job Description

You will be responsible for ensuring the operational integrity and continuous improvement of core business data domains. The role combines ownership of daily data operations, including MDM data supply and issue management, with leadership of data outcomes across change initiatives to ensure data is accurate, controlled, and fit for purpose across the enterprise.

Own the daily operation of the MDM platform, including data ingestion, processing, and controlled execution of the data diffing and reconciliation process to ensure accurate and timely data supply.
Lead the end-to-end management of data requests through Jira Service Management, ensuring effective prioritisation, resolution, root cause linkage, and reduction of recurring issues.
Take accountability for data integrity across domains, ensuring data is accurate, consistent, and aligned to business, regulatory, and operational requirements.
Manage data quality measurement, including definition of rules, monitoring of key quality dimensions, and tracking of metrics such as exception rates, resolution times, data health trends, and overall control effectiveness.
Drive performance against key operational targets, including achieving a zero-diff position, reducing ticket backlog, and improving data quality metrics across domains.
Lead root cause analysis of data issues and implement sustainable remediation actions that address systemic failures and improve data quality at source.
Lead the delivery of data requirements within projects and change initiatives, ensuring data integrity controls, lineage, quality rules, and documentation are fully implemented.
Define and embed data standards and control requirements within MDM processes, data quality rules, and project delivery to ensure consistency and enforceability.
Drive continuous improvement across MDM operations, diffing, and issue management processes, increasing automation and shifting from reactive issue resolution to proactive data control.
Provide clear, outcome-focused reporting on operational performance, including data supply health, diff position, ticket backlog, and data quality metrics to support decision-making.

Qualifications

You Have:

7–10+ years of experience in data management, data operations, or data architecture within large, complex enterprise environments.
Proven experience owning operational data processes, including data supply pipelines, MDM processing, and issue management frameworks.
Experience leading data workstreams within projects or change initiatives, ensuring delivery of data requirements end-to-end.
Strong expertise in master and reference data management, data quality frameworks, metadata, and data governance practices.
Hands-on experience with Jira Service Management or equivalent tools for operational workflow and issue tracking.
Experience with enterprise data tooling such as Informatica, Collibra, Purview, Alation, or similar platforms beneficial.
Advanced SQL and strong hands-on experience working with complex, high-volume datasets.
Proficiency in Python or similar tools to support analysis, validation, and automation.
Deep understanding of end-to-end data flows, including lineage, transformations, integration patterns, and control points.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence business and technology leaders through data-led insights, issue resolution, and delivery of data integrity outcomes across operations and change initiatives.
Experience mentoring team members and driving consistent ways of working across teams.
Experience working in regulated environments such as financial services, risk, or compliance is advantageous.

Additional Information

What’s in it for you to join MUFG Investor Services? 

Take a look at our careers site and you’ll find everything you’d expect working with one of the fastest-growing businesses at one of the world’s largest financial groups. Now take another look. Because it’s how we defy expectations that really defines us. You’ll feel that difference in all kinds of ways.  Our vibrant CULTURE. Connected team. Love of innovation, laser client focus. 

So, why settle for the ordinary?  Apply now for your next Brilliantly Different opportunity.

All AI recommendations are reviewed by our recruitment team before any decisions are made.

More information on our use of AI tools is available in our Privacy Notice available to you as part of your application.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
The Nova Scotia Nursing and Midwifery Regulator
(NSNMR) protects the public by regulating licensed practical nurses, registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, nurse practitioners, and registered midwives across Nova Scotia.

As the largest health profession regulator in Atlantic Canada, NSNMR is entering a pivotal stage in its evolution. Building on the transition to the Regulated Health Professions Act and the integration of nursing and midwifery regulation, the organization is focused on strengthening its operational foundations, modernizing systems and processes, advancing data-informed decision making, and positioning itself as a leading regulator within the region.

To support this important work, NSNMR is seeking a Director of Finance
.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a strategic and collaborative finance leader to contribute to an organization dedicated to public protection and regulatory excellence. The Director of Finance will help guide the organization's long-term financial sustainability while providing the financial insight, stewardship, and leadership required to support informed decision-making, effective governance, and organizational success.

The Role

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Services, the Director of Finance provides leadership and oversight for NSNMR's financial operations, planning, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls. As a member of the leadership team, the Director serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board, providing strategic financial guidance that supports effective decision-making, strong governance, and long-term organizational sustainability. Working closely with leaders across the organization, the Director helps ensure financial resources are aligned with strategic priorities and supports a culture of accountability, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Leading NSNMR's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes to support organizational priorities and long-term sustainability.
Providing strategic financial advice and analysis to support executive and Board decision-making, governance, and resource allocation.
Overseeing all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, investments, cash management, audit, and financial reporting.
Ensuring effective financial controls, compliance practices, and risk management frameworks are in place to safeguard organizational resources.
Supporting organizational planning and performance by translating financial information into meaningful insights for leaders across the organization.
Building and maintaining productive relationships with the Board, auditors, financial institutions, and other external partners.
Leading and developing the finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate Profile

As the ideal candidate, you are a strategic and accomplished finance leader with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and progressive experience leading finance functions within complex organizations. You bring expertise in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls, along with experience providing financial advice and insight to senior leaders and Boards.

You combine strong financial stewardship with sound business judgment and a collaborative leadership style. Comfortable navigating complexity and change, you use financial insight to support decision-making, long-term planning, and organizational sustainability.

An effective communicator and relationship builder, you excel at translating complex financial information into practical insights and building trusted partnerships with colleagues, executives, Board members, and external stakeholders. Experience in a regulated, healthcare, public sector, or not-for-profit environment would be considered an asset.

How to Apply

If you are interested in pursuing this exciting opportunity, please apply by visiting our website https://www.kbrs.ca/Career/17866390385010000008wjg. For more information or to ask any questions, please contact Daniella Sam at dsam@kbrs.ca or Erin MacDonald at emacdonald@kbrs.ca .

Diversity and Accessibility Statement

The Nova Scotia Nursing and Midwifery Regulator is committed to being an organization where diversity and different perspectives are valued. They strive to be an organization that is inclusive, supportive, and reflective of the communities and organizations they serve and encourage applications from candidates who identify as part of a traditionally marginalized community.

KBRS will provide support in its recruitment processes to applicants with disabilities, including accommodation that considers an applicant’s accessibility needs. If you require accommodation to participate as a candidate in the recruitment process, please contact accommodate@kbrs.ca or communicate your needs to our team.

new_jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
new_jobs.description:
Serv, a global executive recruitment partner, is hiring on behalf of our client Martell Ventures for a Chief Technology Officer.

Join the Team:
The Martell Group exists to build people, brands, and ventures that create meaningful impact. Founded by serial entrepreneur and investor Dan Martell, we combine audience, operators, and execution to launch and scale products in Media, B2B SaaS, and AI.

Martell Ventures is a software and AI company that happens to have two services companies in it. Dan is also an investor in companies like Udemy, Intercom, and Unbounce. Our values: Build the people. Be the example. Simple scales.

For more information, visit: https://www.danmartell.com/
Why you shouldn't work here: Radical Transparency from our CEO

Position Responsibilities:
Martell Ventures is looking for a highly technical builder and strategic thinker to lead engineering excellence across its growing portfolio of businesses.

This is not a traditional CTO role focused solely on executive oversight. We need someone who can think strategically, challenge assumptions, and get directly involved in the technical work when it matters most.

You will be the technical authority across the Ventures portfolio, helping companies build better products, solve complex engineering challenges, strengthen technical teams, and move faster with modern AI and agentic development.

You'll work closely with Dan Martell, portfolio business leaders, and experienced technology advisors to turn ambitious ideas into practical, scalable solutions.

A significant part of your mandate will be establishing Martell Ventures' technical presence in Waterloo, building a strong local engineering community, and creating the standards that enable our portfolio companies to scale.

This is an opportunity to shape how multiple businesses build, operate, and grow while remaining close to the technology itself.

This role includes:
Technical Strategy & Architecture
Evaluate the technical infrastructure, architecture, codebases, and engineering practices across portfolio companies, identifying opportunities to improve quality, security, scalability, and performance.
Work directly with engineering teams to diagnose technical challenges, improve architecture, and implement practical solutions.
Establish consistent engineering standards, shared development practices, frameworks, and tooling across the portfolio.
Drive adoption of modern AI and agentic development practices to improve engineering speed, efficiency, and product delivery.
Ensure portfolio companies maintain appropriate technical infrastructure, security practices, backups, and operational resilience.
Help portfolio leaders understand technical risks, opportunities, and priorities so they can make informed business decisions.
Support technical readiness for future acquisitions, investment opportunities, and potential exits.

Building & Developing Technical Talent
Establish and grow Martell Ventures' technical presence in Kitchener-Waterloo.
Help recruit, assess, and develop exceptional engineering talent across the portfolio.
Partner with portfolio business leaders on technical hiring decisions, including engineering leads and senior technical positions.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to portfolio engineering leaders while maintaining a dotted-line relationship with those leaders.
Establish consistent technical practices, knowledge-sharing, and training opportunities across portfolio teams.
Develop relationships with the University of Waterloo, Communitech, and the broader Waterloo technology ecosystem to build a sustainable talent pipeline.
Collaborate with Waterloo-based technology advisors Michael Litt and Marcelo Cortes to strengthen the group's engineering capabilities and local network.

Product Development & Execution
Translate ambitious business ideas into practical technical plans with clear priorities, realistic timelines, and measurable outcomes.
Provide hands-on technical support when portfolio companies face complex engineering challenges or execution bottlenecks.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions and help prioritize technical investments based on business value.
Support engineering teams in delivering reliable, scalable products that meet customer needs.
Identify opportunities to share technical capabilities, infrastructure, and resources across portfolio businesses.
Balance long-term technical architecture with the immediate needs of fast-moving businesses.

Strategic Partnership & Leadership
Serve as a trusted technical thought partner to Dan Martell and the Ventures leadership team.
Bring independent technical judgment, including the confidence to challenge ideas, push back on unrealistic commitments, and recommend alternative approaches.
Help establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Work across multiple businesses and priorities while maintaining a clear focus on the highest-impact opportunities.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, and progress clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Lead by example through a combination of strategic thinking, practical execution, and strong technical credibility.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone with exceptional technical depth, strong product judgment, and the ability to build in fast-moving environments.
You may have held a CTO or VP of Engineering position, or you may be an exceptional Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or technical founder ready to take on broader responsibility.

What matters most is your ability to solve difficult technical problems, raise engineering standards, and build products that work.
Deep hands-on experience in software engineering, systems architecture, and building scalable production applications.
Recent, practical experience developing with modern AI technologies, LLMs, agents, and agentic development tools.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate existing software architecture, identify technical weaknesses, and implement effective solutions.
Strong technical credibility and the ability to work directly with experienced engineers on complex technical challenges.
Experience building and shipping software products in startup, scale-up, or similarly fast-moving environments.
Strong product and business judgment, with an understanding of how technical decisions affect customers, revenue, and growth.
Experience assessing engineering talent, making technical hiring decisions, and helping build high-performing teams.
Ability to balance technical quality with speed, pragmatism, and commercial priorities.
Confidence working with strong founder personalities and challenging ideas when necessary.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business recommendations.
High ownership, adaptability, and comfort operating across multiple businesses with changing priorities.
Based in, or willing to relocate to, Kitchener-Waterloo and work in person full-time.

Nice-to-Haves
Previous experience as a CTO, technical co-founder, VP of Engineering, or senior technical leader.
Experience supporting multiple products, portfolio companies, or venture-backed businesses.
Experience building or scaling an engineering function from an early stage.
Involvement in a successful company exit or technical due diligence process.
Existing connections within the Waterloo technology ecosystem, including the University of Waterloo or Communitech.
Experience establishing engineering standards and shared infrastructure across multiple teams.

Our Dream Teammate Is Someone Who:
Is a builder at heart and genuinely enjoys getting into the technical details.
Is excited by the pace of change in AI and is actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Can move comfortably between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
Knows when to challenge an idea, when to simplify a solution, and when to move quickly.
Has strong technical opinions but remains open to learning and feedback.
Thrives in entrepreneurial environments where priorities evolve and ownership matters.
Is proactive and accountable.
Thinks strategically and executes consistently.
Communicates with clarity and confidence.
Brings a positive, growth-oriented mindset.
Is highly organized and dependable.
Cares deeply about building great products and developing great people.

Hiring Process
We take our hiring process seriously and evaluate candidates based on both capability and culture fit. Our goal is to ensure you step into a role where you feel genuinely excited and fulfilled. That's important for you, and it's equally important for us.

Below is a snapshot of what you can expect throughout our hiring process.

Please note that steps may vary slightly depending on the position.
Initial application review and introductory conversation with Serv.
Leadership and culture-fit conversation with Martell Ventures.
Technical evaluation with members of the Martell Ventures technical leadership or advisory network.
Final-stage conversations with key stakeholders.

Location
Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Canada

This is a full-time, in-person position. The CTO will play a central role in establishing and leading Martell Ventures' Waterloo technical hub.

Compensation
$150,000- $250,000 CAD base, based on experience.

The opportunity also includes a proposed portfolio-level phantom equity component designed to align long-term incentives with the performance and success of the Ventures portfolio. Final terms are subject to confirmation.
This isn't just a job. It's a platform to build, grow, and win.

Serv uses AI tools in our recruitment process, including developing job postings and note-taking during interviews. AI is not used to screen, assess, or select candidates. All resumes are reviewed by a human, and all hiring decisions are made by humans. Any AI-generated output used during the recruitment process is reviewed by a human before action is taken.
